_note: How each region and province plays (src/provinceRules.ts, docs/ONLINE_PLAN.md 5.2). Each layer lists only what it changes: the game's defaults, then the region's, then the province's. Multipliers are 0.1-5 (1 = as the game is), months are 1-12, chancePerMonth is 0-1, drought.share (how much less a water works gives in a dry-season month, when only rain or a storm fills the ground, a little) is 0-0.9. weather (src/weather.ts) lists twelve numbers 0-1 for each month, January first: rain, the chance the month is wet; storm, the share of wet months that are storms (heavy rain); fog, the share of dry months that are foggy; smoke, the haze of burning fields and forests; and flood, the chance a storm month floods low land beside the water (only while disasters are on). festivals (src/festivals.ts) adds a region's or province's festivals to the country's own (New Year, Songkran, Loy Krathong), by id, each with its month 1-12 and any of its numbers to change (draw, homecoming, waterUse, and pairs for modest and grand: cost, land, fire, rubbish, dirt; cheer has not held, modest, grand); null takes one away. Edited by the owner; once the game is online the same data lives in the server's database and an admin page edits it.

north._note: Tourism: shops are wanted. Thick forest: clearing woods costs more. Yi Peng's sky lanterns rise with Loy Krathong.

northeast._note: Cheap land and farm industry. Droughts: a long dry season for the water works, fires in the hot season. Bun Bang Fai's rockets ask the sky for the rains in May.

central._note: Trade: shops are wanted. Floods in the rainy season.

west._note: Hydropower: power plants give more. Little flat land: roads and rail cost more.

south._note: Tourism and seaports. Storms at the end of the year. The vegetarian festival in October.

provinces._note: Changes for one province over its region, e.g. "TH-83": { "demand": { "commercial": 1.6 } } for Phuket. A province that lists seasons replaces its region's list; one that lists weather replaces only the lists it gives, and festivals only the festivals it names.

TH-40._note: Khon Kaen: the silk festival and Phuk Siao, late November into December, counted in December.

TH-85._note: Ranong, on the Andaman coast: the southwest monsoon's rains, May to October, not the east coast's.
